claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
The nanoparticles initially form a chemically uniform, disordered solid-solution phase.
Stability from 473 to 1923 K is governed by the balance between configurational entropy and lattice distortion caused by atomic-size mismatch.
At moderate lattice distortion, high configurational entropy kinetically suppresses diffusion-driven ordering and phase separation.
Above a lattice-strain threshold, enthalpic driving forces for ordering or segregation overcome entropy stabilization.
Low- and high-distortion nanoparticle groups can be identical in composition while being made from constituent metals with different atomic-size disparities.
Flash heating followed by quenching can produce an initially homogeneous solid solution.
Using an inert or controlled reactive atmosphere avoids additional environmental effects during thermal testing.
Changes in lattice distortion can be measured through XRD-derived lattice parameters.
Short-range chemical order can be assessed using EXAFS and atomistic TEM imaging.
High configurational entropy stabilizes disordered solid solutions by lowering their Gibbs free energy relative to ordered phases.
Atomic-size mismatch creates lattice strain that can enhance atomic mobility.
Local lattice distortions provide sites for incipient chemical ordering.
Competition between entropy stabilization and distortion-driven ordering determines nanoparticle structural stability at high temperature.
Nanoparticles with lower atomic-size mismatch will retain a single-phase, chemically homogeneous solid solution throughout 473–1923 K operation.
Retention of structural and chemical homogeneity will preserve both catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
Nanoparticles with higher atomic-size mismatch will exhibit more short-range ordering or phase segregation.
Ordering or segregation in the high-distortion group will produce altered XRD peak shapes or secondary phases.
Ordering or phase segregation caused by high lattice distortion will degrade catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
Atomic-size differences below roughly 15% constitute an acceptable threshold for the predicted stability behavior.

contradictions.description: The groups are said to be identical in composition while also being selected from different constituent metals to create different atomic-size mismatches. Changing elemental constituents changes composition unless 'composition' only means equal-ratio stoichiometry.

The hypothesis predicts instability when strain exceeds a threshold, but the stated applicability condition says the prediction should hold when size differences remain below the acceptable threshold. This makes the intended domain of the high-distortion comparison ambiguous.
